material_systems.name: Acrylic Wood Primer

products: Benjamin Moore Fresh Start All-Purpose Primer
primer.notes: Standard acrylic primer for bare wood windows. Good adhesion to sanded wood. Fast dry. For knots or tannin bleed, use shellac-based spot primer (SYS_PRIMER_WOOD_SHELLAC) before this system coat.

material_systems.notes: Substrate-driven primer selection per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 3. Applies only when substrate_state = SS_BARE. SS_PRIMED_FACTORY skips primer.

material_systems.name: Shellac-Based Knot/Tannin Primer

primer.notes: Spot primer for knots, tannin bleed, and stain blocking on bare wood. Apply to affected areas before system primer coat. Fast dry (15-45 min).

material_systems.notes: Spot application only — not full surface. Used before acrylic primer on problem areas.

material_systems.name: DTM Etching Primer for Aluminum

products: PPG Pitt-Tech DTM Industrial Enamel Primer
primer.notes: Requires thorough degreasing and chemical etch/mechanical abrasion before application. Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.2. Organofunctional silane or phosphoric acid pre-treatment recommended for maximum adhesion.

material_systems.notes: Substrate-driven. Always required for aluminum windows regardless of substrate_state — aluminum oxide layer requires adhesion primer.

material_systems.name: Rust-Inhibitive DTM Primer for Steel

products: Rust-Oleum Professional High Performance Rust Preventive Primer
PPG Pitt-Tech Plus DTM Industrial Primer
primer.notes: Requires thorough degreasing, rust assessment per SSPC standards, and mechanical/chemical rust treatment before application. Flash-rust prevention critical — apply immediately after prep in humid conditions. Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.3.4.

material_systems.notes: Substrate-driven. Contains zinc, red oxide, or other corrosion inhibitors. Always required for steel windows.

material_systems.name: Standard Acrylic Trim Enamel

products: Sherwin-Williams ProClassic Waterborne Interior Acrylic Enamel
Benjamin Moore Regal Select Interior Semi-Gloss
finish.notes: Fast dry/recoat. Non-yellowing. Water cleanup. Standard production grade. Same system as trim spec.

material_systems.notes: Standard production system for QT3. Satin is the only sheen at QT3 per sheen/QT gate. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Modified Urethane Trim Enamel

products: Benjamin Moore Advance Waterborne Interior Alkyd
Sherwin-Williams Pro Industrial Waterbased Alkyd Urethane
finish.notes: Superior flow and leveling. SHORT working time — apply, tip once, walk away. Sands easily between coats. Same system as trim spec.

material_systems.notes: Premium residential for QT4. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Premium Urethane Trim Enamel

finish.coat_notes: QT5 brush/roll typically requires 3+ coats per FFD 15.10.3.
finish.notes: Maximum durability. Excellent leveling. Emerald Urethane is acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT waterborne alkyd (RC-006). Same system as trim spec.

material_systems.notes: Premium/custom home for QT5. Gloss available only at this tier. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

coverage_profiles.notes: Window primer coverage. Material quantity derived from window count × estimated SF per window using size bucket perimeter math (Area = P²÷16). Includes frame, sash, muntin, jamb surfaces. Metal primers may have slightly lower coverage.
assumptions: Bare substrate (SS_BARE for wood, bare metal for aluminum/steel)
Coverage varies by substrate: wood absorbs more (lower coverage) than metal (higher coverage)

coverage_profiles.notes: Window finish coverage on primed smooth surface. Material quantity derived from window count × estimated SF per window. Two-coat standard; third coat at QT5 brush/roll has same per-coat coverage. Spray method: add 20-40% material waste for overspray per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 8.2.2.
assumptions: Standard window complexity. Multi-pane (TDL) has more surface area — lower effective coverage per window.
Spray waste factor (20-40%) is additional — not included in base coverage rate.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150-grit
consumables.notes: 150 grit for initial bare wood sanding before primer. Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 3.2.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220-grit
consumables.usage: Pre-primer final sand (wood), between-coat sanding (QT3 spot, QT4 full)
consumables.notes: 220 grit for final bare wood sand, factory primer scuff, and between-coat sanding. Rigid sanding block mandatory for defect removal (FFD 15.4.1).

consumables.name: Sandpaper 320-grit
consumables.notes: 220-320 grit range at QT5. Uniform scratch pattern required. Rigid sanding block mandatory (FFD 15.4.1).

consumables.name: Sanding block (fine grit range)
consumables.usage: Rigid block for between-coat sanding. Mandatory per FFD 15.4.1.
consumables.notes: One block per crew, reusable across coats and windows.

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (1.5")
consumables.usage: Primary brush for window detail work (sash, muntins, frame details)
consumables.notes: 1.5-inch angled sash brush per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 8.2.1. Smaller than trim brush (2-2.5") for detailed window profiles. One per painter per material change.

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (2-2.5")
consumables.usage: Secondary brush for larger window frame surfaces and extension jamb
consumables.notes: 2-2.5 inch for flat frame faces and extension jamb. One per painter.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 310-411
consumables.usage: Fine atomization for window spray finish
consumables.notes: Tight fan pattern for window work.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.usage: Remove sanding dust before each coat application
consumables.notes: One tack cloth covers ~8 medium windows. Use before every coat.

consumables.name: Masking tape (1.5" blue painter's tape)
consumables.usage: Glass edge masking, wall masking, hardware masking
consumables.notes: 60 yards = 180 LF per roll. Primary masking tape for all protection tasks.

consumables.name: Glass masking film/paper
consumables.usage: Cover glass panes to protect from paint
consumables.notes: Pre-taped masking film or masking paper cut to pane size. Mandatory for all windows.

consumables.name: Masking paper (12")
consumables.usage: Wall masking adjacent to window during spray
consumables.notes: 60 yards = 180 LF per roll. Wall adjacent masking for spray method.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloth
consumables.usage: Floor protection in window work area
consumables.notes: Runner-style for brush, full coverage for spray. Reusable. Required when floor_type = finished or partial.

consumables.name: Single-edge razor blade
consumables.notes: Sharp razor for scraping excess paint from glass during cleanup. Replace frequently for clean cuts. Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 4.1.1.

consumables.name: Sandable wood filler
consumables.usage: Fill wood grain defects, nail holes, minor damage on bare wood windows
consumables.notes: Sandable filler for bare wood prep. Lightweight or auto-body type depending on defect depth.

consumables.name: Alkaline degreaser (BC-7000 or equivalent)
consumables.usage: Degrease metal window surfaces before prep
consumables.notes: Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.1: all metal substrates require thorough degreasing before mechanical/chemical prep.

consumables.name: Phosphoric acid rust converter
consumables.usage: Convert iron oxide to stable iron phosphate on steel windows
consumables.notes: Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.3.3. Products: Ospho, POR-15 Metal Prep. Product turns black when conversion is complete.

floor_perimeter.description: Drop cloth runners along window work area (brush method)
floor_perimeter.condition: application_method = brush AND floor_type = finished or partial

floor_full_8ft_radius.description: Full radial floor coverage around window spray zone
floor_full_8ft_radius.condition: application_method = spray AND floor_type = finished or partial

glass_mask.description: Paper/film masking on all window glass panes

wall_adjacent_window.condition: application_method = spray, or walls are SS_PAINTED_*

sill_protection.condition: application_method = spray AND stool is SS_PAINTED_*

compatibility_rules.description: All finish systems are compatible with all primer systems
compatibility_rules.notes: Primer and finish are independent selections. All combinations valid.

compatibility_rules.description: SS_PRIMED_FACTORY compatible with all finish systems
compatibility_rules.notes: Scuff sand factory primer for adhesion. No additional primer needed.

risk_notes.risk: Freshly painted windows stuck closed due to insufficient cure time
risk_notes.mitigation: Paint sashes in ajar position. Allow 3-7 day cure before closing. Use urethane-enriched enamels for blocking resistance. Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 10.1.

risk_notes.risk: Paint peels from aluminum or steel due to inadequate prep
risk_notes.mitigation: Thorough degreasing. Chemical etch for aluminum. Rust treatment for steel. Use DTM primer system. Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Sections 6.2, 6.3.

risk_notes.risk: Bare steel rusts between prep and priming in humid conditions
risk_notes.mitigation: Apply primer immediately after prep. Use flash-rust inhibiting primers. Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.3.4.

risk_notes.risk: Overworking causes roping, brush marks on window surfaces
risk_notes.mitigation: Apply, tip once, walk away (FFD 15.3.1). Sand marks out between coats with rigid block.

material_notes.dual_system_architecture: This spec has TWO independent material system layers: (1) Primer systems are substrate-driven (wood, aluminum, steel). (2) Finish systems are QT-driven. Any primer can pair with any finish system.
material_notes.coverage_note: Coverage is SF-based but quantity is EA-derived. Use size bucket perimeter math (Area = P²÷16) to estimate SF per window, multiply by window count. Spray method adds 20-40% waste factor.
material_notes.brush_size_note: 1.5-inch angled sash brush for detail work (sash, muntins). 2-2.5 inch for larger frame faces and extension jamb. Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 8.2.1.
material_notes.product_classification: Advance is waterborne alkyd. Emerald Urethane is acrylic-urethane enamel (RC-006).

assumptions.value: 350-450 SF/gal for finish coat on primed smooth window surface
assumptions.source: Manufacturer PDS data, aligned with trim spec coverage
